name: Carvajal Syndrome
aliases: Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Woolly Hair and Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of dilated cardiomyopathy confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Diffuse palmoplantar keratoderma typically developing in infancy or early childhood
Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the DSP gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: dilated cardiomyopathy, woolly hair, and palmoplantar keratoderma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for DSP mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical criteria are met.

pathognomonic.notes: Leads to heart failure and arrhythmias
Fine, tightly curled hair present from birth or early infancy
Diffuse thickening of skin on palms and soles

searchTerms: symptoms of heart failure like breathlessness
fatigue and shortness of breath from heart problems

common.notes: Includes ventricular tachycardia and sudden cardiac death risk
Due to muscle weakness secondary to cardiomyopathy

occasional.notes: May occur due to myocardial ischemia

rare.notes: Patchy hair loss beyond woolly hair

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing dilated left ventricle with reduced ejection fraction
Cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial fibrosis and ventricular dilation
other: Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis and acanthosis in palmoplantar keratoderma

distinguishingFeatures: Associated with woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma

redFlags: Early onset heart failure symptoms in a child with skin and hair abnormalities
Family history of sudden cardiac death
Presence of ventricular arrhythmias or syncope
references: Carvajal-Huerta L. A form of cardiocutaneous syndrome with woolly hair and keratoderma. Br J Dermatol. 1998.
Protonotarios N, Tsatsopoulou A. Naxos disease: cardiocutaneous syndrome due to cell adhesion defect. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2006.

McKoy G, Protonotarios N, Crosby A, et al. Identification of a deletion in plakoglobin in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair (Naxos disease). Lancet. 2000.
